title: Grammar Edit — Sentence Repair
description: Practice choosing the correct edit for each underlined section.
subject: rla

questions.prompt: The manager, along with the two new hires, {{blank}} attending the safety training on Monday.

options.whyWrong: “Are” matches a plural subject, but the true subject here is the singular noun “manager.”
The tense shifts unnecessarily. The sentence calls for a present-tense verb, not past tense.
This verb phrase changes both number and tense, making the sentence grammatically off target.

questions.explanation: The subject is 'the manager' (singular) — the phrase 'along with the two new hires' doesn't change subject-verb agreement, so the verb stays singular: 'is'.
questions.rule: Ignore interrupting phrases like “along with ...” when deciding whether the verb should be singular or plural.

questions.prompt: The two engineers reviewed {{blank}} notes before the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Their' is the possessive determiner that correctly shows the notes belong to the two engineers. 'There' refers to a place, and 'they’re' means 'they are'.
questions.rule: Check what job the word must do in the sentence. Before a noun like “notes,” you need a possessive determiner.
